extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematics students, and researchers interested in mathematical creativity, problem-solving, and the psychology of invention
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for judging the quality of mathematical work and the conditions that produce good mathematics, drawn from Hadamard's empirical account of discovery (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) and associated habits of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation (sustained conscious labor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained, conscious labor: defining the problem, surveying tools, attempting standard approaches; long preparation precedes insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence the author mastered prior tools and attempted standard approaches before the new idea appeared. Anti-patterns: apparent shortcuts or skipping background work — 'shortcuts that skip preparation produce shallow work.' Scoring note: absence of demonstrated preparation weakens claims of novelty or depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incubation (putting the problem away)
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem is 'put away'; unconscious combinatorial work proceeds and the mind continues to recombine ideas outside conscious focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work or the author's account allows for periods of rest or incubation (e.g., problems set aside between attempts). Practical guidance: sustained focus should be interleaved with rest; treating discovery as purely continuous conscious grind is suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illumination (sudden appearance of the idea)
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer or the key idea appears suddenly in consciousness — a flash of insight marking the moment of discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize illumination as a legitimate psychological stage but not as a substitute for verification. Works that claim a 'magic' insight without prior preparation or subsequent checking should be treated cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification (conscious checking and formalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conscious checking, formalization, and writing up of the discovered idea to produce a rigorous, communicable result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require independent verification of the result separate from the discovery narrative: formal proofs, checks of special cases, and clear exposition. The page warns: 'A solution presented without evidence of stages 1 or 4 is suspect.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic-selection filter (elegance/harmony/usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unconscious does not deliver random combinations; it favors combinations that are elegant, harmonious, or useful — an aesthetic filter that selects what reaches consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive evidence: final solutions show 'clean structure' and lack traces of false starts. Anti-patterns: proofs that preserve many ad-hoc tinkering steps in their final form. Scoring note: aesthetic quality (clarity, structural harmony, parsimony) is a substantive indicator of mature mathematical thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean final form (no false starts retained)
rubrics_metrics.description: A worked solution that retains traces of the unconscious aesthetic filter appears in a clean form, without the false starts or aborted approaches visible in the final write-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge final exposition for elimination of clutter: a good piece of mathematics often hides messy exploration. If the final text preserves a patchwork of dead ends, it suggests weaker selection and lower maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery rather than verbalism (visual/spatial/kinesthetic thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Productive mathematical thought is rarely word-by-word verbal; it is typically visual, spatial, or kinesthetic in character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value explanations or proofs that reveal an underlying geometric or structural image. Anti-pattern: heavy reliance on literal verbal reasoning or stepwise textual manipulation without an accompanying mental image — Hadamard found this suspect among practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for vagueness in the exploratory phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Vagueness is essential: productive mathematicians work with imprecise images that are later sharpened into precise arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penalize preliminary imprecision in heuristics or informal notes; such vagueness often fosters invention. Conversely, demanding full formal precision at every exploratory step 'blocks invention' and can produce sterile work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between logic of discovery and logic of justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer should distinguish the psychological/creative path that led to the idea (logic of discovery) from the formal, justificatory presentation (logic of justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect papers or expositions to separate anecdotal insight accounts from rigorous proofs. Conflating the two (presenting the discovery narrative as if it were the proof) can confuse evaluation and obscure logical gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep preparation / mastery of prior tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work show evidence of deep preparation — mastery of prior results, tools, and relevant literature that populate the mind with combinations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for citations, background lemmas, or demonstration of familiarity with standard techniques that the new work builds upon. Scoring: works lacking demonstration of background mastery are less convincing as substantive advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained focus interleaved with rest (productive practice condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained focused work combined with periods of rest (allowing incubation) is a condition for mathematical productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims of productivity against reported work rhythms: long sessions punctuated by breaks/other activity are consistent with Hadamard's account. Anti-pattern: claims of continuous rapid invention without rest are psychologically implausible under this model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of knowledge enabling novel combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A mind populated with a wide stock of 'combinations' — broad mathematical knowledge — increases the chance of creating novel connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the breadth of tools and domains the work draws on; interdisciplinary or wide-ranging background increases plausibility of genuinely novel combinations rather than accidental reworkings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivated aesthetic taste (training of the unconscious filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic training and mathematical taste improve the quality of the unconscious selection mechanism and thereby the quality of discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the author's demonstrated taste (choice of clean formulations, preference for structural clarity) as a positive signal. Training in aesthetic judgment can be as relevant as technical skill for producing high-quality mathematics.
